bib.title: Self-training with Noisy Student improves ImageNet classification

question: Can self-training with an equal-or-larger, noised student on large unlabeled image data improve ImageNet accuracy and robustness beyond supervised and weakly-supervised SOTA?
hypothesis: Noising the student (augmentation, dropout, stochastic depth) and making it at least as large as the teacher lets the student exceed the teacher.
contributions: Noisy Student Training: self-training with equal-or-larger student and injected noise
Large robustness gains on ImageNet-A, C, P and FGSM/PGD attacks without optimising for robustness

method.summary: Train a teacher EfficientNet on labeled ImageNet, pseudo-label filtered/balanced unlabeled JFT images with the un-noised teacher, then train an equal-or-larger EfficientNet student jointly on labeled and pseudo-labeled data with noise (RandAugment, dropout, stochastic depth); iterate with the student as new teacher.

datasets.name: ImageNet 2012 ILSVRC
datasets.split: train for labeled data; validation set for eval

datasets.name: JFT (labels ignored)
datasets.preprocessing: ImageNet val images removed; EfficientNet-B0 labels each image; keep confidence >0.3; at most 130K highest-confidence per class; duplicate to 130K for smaller classes

datasets.name: YFCC100M
datasets.preprocessing: same filtering as JFT, top 130K per class by B0 top-1

datasets.name: SVHN
datasets.size: 73K core set labeled; 531K extra set unlabeled
datasets.split: core set as train and validation

datasets.name: ImageNet-A / C / P
datasets.preprocessing: C and P evaluated at 224 and 299 resolution

models.name: EfficientNet-L2
models.architecture: EfficientNet scaled up from B7, w=4.3 d=5.3, train res 475, test res 800
models.init_from: inferred: from scratch (warm-start from teacher not used; Study 8)

training.objective: cross entropy on labeled plus soft pseudo-labeled (hard also works) images, averaged over concatenated batch; teacher un-noised when labeling
training.lr_schedule: decay 0.97 every 2.4 epochs (350-epoch runs) or every 4.8 epochs (700-epoch runs)
training.batch_size: labeled 2048 by default (reduced if memory-bound); unlabeled batch 3x labeled for B1-B7 sweep, 14x then 28x for L2
training.epochs: 350 for models larger than B4 including L2; 700 for smaller
training.regularisation: stochastic depth survival prob 0.8 at final layer, linear decay; RandAugment 2 ops magnitude 27 (ResNet-50: magnitude 9)
training.wall_clock: 6 days for EfficientNet-L2 with unlabeled batch 14x labeled

other.fixres: L2: train 350 epochs at smaller resolution, then finetune 1.5 epochs at larger res on unaugmented labeled images with shallow layers fixed

inference.samples: single reported number per model; no seeds or repeats stated

parameters.adversarial: FGSM, and PGD with 10 iterations at epsilon 16; input resolution 800x800

metrics.name: mCE
metrics.definition: weighted average error on ImageNet-C corruptions normalised by AlexNet error

metrics.name: mFR
metrics.definition: mean flip rate of top-1 prediction under ImageNet-P perturbations, normalised by AlexNet

eval.protocol: single run per config, no significance test stated

results.claim: Noisy Student EfficientNet-L2 reaches 88.4% ImageNet top-1 versus 86.4% for FixRes ResNeXt-101 WSL (3.5B Instagram images).
results.setup: ImageNet 2012 val, EfficientNet-L2 student, 300M unlabeled JFT images (130M after filter/balance), 3 iterations
results.table: Table 2, row Noisy Student Training (EfficientNet-L2), column Top-1 Acc.; 86.4% row FixRes ResNeXt-101 WSL

results.claim: Gain over EfficientNet-B7 85.0% splits into +0.5% from bigger model and +2.9% from Noisy Student.
results.quote: by making the model larger (+0.5%) and by Noisy Student Training (+2.9%)

results.claim: ImageNet-A top-1 rises from 49.6% (supervised L2) and 61.0% (prior SOTA) to 83.7%.
results.table: Table 3, row Noisy Student Training (L2), column Top-1 Acc.

results.claim: ImageNet-C mCE falls to 28.3 from 45.7 (prior SOTA) at 299 resolution.
results.table: Table 4, row Noisy Student Training (L2) 299, column mCE

results.claim: ImageNet-P mFR falls to 12.2 from 27.8 at 299 resolution (14.2 at 224).
results.table: Table 5, row Noisy Student Training (L2) 299, column mFR

results.claim: Consistent gain around 0.8% for every EfficientNet size B0-B7 with same-size teacher, no iteration.
results.setup: B0-B7, unlabeled batch 3x labeled (1x for B0)
results.quote: Training leads to a consistent improvement of around 0.8%

results.claim: Removing noise on unlabeled data drops B5 from 85.1% to 84.3% (130M unlabeled), barely above the 84.0% supervised baseline.
results.setup: B5 teacher and student, 130M unlabeled, no iteration
results.table: Table 6, row student w/o Aug, SD, Dropout, column 130M

results.claim: Iterative training: 87.6% then 88.1% then 88.4% (last with 28:1 unlabeled ratio).
Under PGD 10 steps at epsilon 16, accuracy of L2 improves from 1.1% to 4.4%.

results.claim: Using the 88.4% L2 model as teacher gets B4 to 85.3%.
results.setup: B4 student, L2 teacher, standard augmentation, 700 epochs
results.table: Table 9, row Noisy Student Training (B4, L2)

results.claim: With public YFCC100M instead of JFT, B7 reaches 86.2% versus 86.4% on JFT.
results.table: Table 18, row Noisy Student Training (B7) YFCC

results.claim: Joint training beats pretrain-then-finetune: B0 77.9% vs 77.5%.
results.table: Table 13, row Joint Training, column B0

limits: Unlabeled data is Google-internal JFT; public YFCC100M gives slightly lower results.
Single runs, no seeds or error bars; optimizer and precision not stated.
Compute heavy: L2 needs 6 days on a 2048-core TPU v3 Pod.
Authors note RandAugment overlaps slightly with ImageNet-C/P corruptions (brightness, contrast, sharpness).
Adversarial results not comparable to prior work due to 800x800 input.
Hard vs soft pseudo labels must be chosen case by case.

terms.definition: self-training with an equal-or-larger student and noise added to the student during learning

lineage.work: Yalniz et al. billion-scale semi-supervised learning
lineage.note: self-training baseline; pretrain then finetune vs joint training here
soft targets, but student not smaller and noised

figures.caption: Illustration of the Noisy Student Training.

figures.caption: Noisy Student Training leads to significant improvements across all model sizes.

code.snippet: 1: Learn teacher; 2: pseudo-label clean unlabeled images with un-noised teacher; 3: train equal-or-larger noised student on labeled + pseudo-labeled; 4: student becomes teacher
